title: Part 3 Practice: Cloud, Quantum, Autonomic Computing & Computer Vision

questions.text: What are the three main types of cloud infrastructure mentioned in the module?
options: A) Public, Private, and Hybrid Cloud.
B) Local, Remote, and Global Cloud.
C) Small, Medium, and Large Cloud.
D) Free, Paid, and Premium Cloud.
questions.correct_answer: A) Public, Private, and Hybrid Cloud.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'One of the following three types of cloud infrastructure is used: The first type is a public cloud... A business or organization would typically use a private cloud... The third option is a hybrid cloud.'

questions.text: What is the 'economy of scale' advantage of cloud computing?
options: A) It makes computing more expensive.
B) It provides cheap computing power because hardware and software are shared, eliminating costly capital investment.
C) It forces businesses to buy their own servers.
D) It has no cost benefits.
questions.correct_answer: B) It provides cheap computing power because hardware and software are shared, eliminating costly capital investment.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Much like with any utility, a business benefits from economy of scale, which means cheap computing power. Because a cloud provider's hardware and software are shared, there's no need for the initial costly capital investment.'

questions.text: What is a qubit in quantum computing?
options: A) A bit that only stores the value 0.
B) A sequence of quantum bits that can exist in two states (1 and 0) at the same time due to superposition.
C) A physical wire that connects computers.
D) A type of cloud storage.
questions.correct_answer: B) A sequence of quantum bits that can exist in two states (1 and 0) at the same time due to superposition.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Qubit is short for a sequence of quantum bits... With a quantum computer, the data is stored in qubits. Thanks to the mechanics of quantum physics... a qubit can exist in two states at the same time. This phenomenon is called superposition.'

questions.text: Which company provided the fastest quantum computer with 53 qubits, completing a computation in 200 seconds that would take a supercomputer 10,000 years?
options: A) IBM
B) Microsoft
C) Google
D) Amazon
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Not to be outdone, Google provided the fastest quantum computer with 53 qubits and speed of 200 seconds computation while the supercomputer took 10000 years.'

questions.text: What is the goal of Autonomic Computing (AC)?
options: A) To make computers slower.
B) To create systems that run themselves, capable of high-level functioning while keeping the system's complexity invisible to the user.
C) To eliminate all computer systems.
D) To only work on mainframes.
questions.correct_answer: B) To create systems that run themselves, capable of high-level functioning while keeping the system's complexity invisible to the user.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The goal of autonomic computing is to create systems that run themselves, capable of high-level functioning while keeping the system's complexity invisible to the user.'

questions.text: Which characteristic of autonomic systems allows them to detect and recover from potential problems?
options: A) Self-Configuring
B) Self-Healing
C) Self-Optimizing
D) Self-Protecting
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Self-Healing: An autonomic application/system should be able to detect and recover from potential problems and continue to function smoothly.'

questions.text: What are the three main steps of how computer vision works?
options: A) Input, Processing, Output.
B) Acquiring an image, Processing the image, Understanding the image.
C) Scanning, Saving, Printing.
D) Detecting, Analyzing, Deleting.
questions.correct_answer: B) Acquiring an image, Processing the image, Understanding the image.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Computer vision works in three main steps: 1. Acquiring an image... 2. Processing the image... 3. Understanding the image.'

questions.text: What is the first commercial use of computer vision mentioned in the module's history section?
options: A) Facial recognition.
B) Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to interpret text for the blind.
C) Self-driving cars.
D) Video game graphics.
questions.correct_answer: B) Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to interpret text for the blind.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'In the 1970s, the first commercial use of computer vision interpreted typed or handwritten text using optical character recognition. This advancement was used to interpret written text for the blind.'

questions.text: Which technique in computer vision partitions an image into multiple regions to be examined separately?
options: A) Object detection.
B) Image segmentation.
C) Facial recognition.
D) Edge detection.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Image segmentation partitions an image into multiple regions or pieces to be examined separately.'

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT listed as an application of computer vision in the module?
options: A) Optical character recognition (OCR) and automatic number plate recognition (ANPR).
B) Medical imaging and automotive safety.
C) Surveillance and fingerprint recognition.
D) Cloud storage and file sharing.
questions.correct_answer: D) Cloud storage and file sharing.
questions.explanation: The module lists: OCR, Machine inspection, Retail, Medical imaging, Automotive safety, Surveillance, and Fingerprint recognition. Cloud storage is a cloud computing application, not a computer vision application.
